ai.literal: To the destitute something giving indeed is charity; other all, expectation of return nature it possesses.
ai.translation: True charity is giving to the destitute. All other giving has the nature of expecting a return.
ai.modern: வறுமையில் வாடுபவர்களுக்கு ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுப்பதே உண்மையான ஈகையாகும். மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கொடுப்பதெல்லாம், திரும்பப் பெறும் நோக்கத்தைக் கொண்டதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true nature of charity. It states that giving to those who are completely destitute and cannot give anything back is the only real act of giving. Any other kind of giving is essentially a transaction. The phrase 'குறியெதிர்ப்பை' specifically refers to expecting a measured return, highlighting that conditional giving is not true charity.

ai.literal: Good path even if, receiving is bad; higher world does not exist even if, giving alone is good.
ai.translation: Even if receiving is considered a good path, it is bad. Even if there is no higher world, giving alone is good.
ai.modern: பிறரிடம் இருந்து பொருளைப் பெறுவது நல்ல வழி என்று சொல்லப்பட்டாலும் அது தீமையானது. மேலுலகம் இல்லை என்று சொல்லப்பட்டாலும் பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதே நன்மையானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the inherent nature of receiving and giving. The word 'நல்லாறு' (good path) suggests that even if taking from others is justified as a righteous or acceptable way to live, it remains inherently bad. Conversely, even if one believes there is no 'மேலுலகம்' (higher world or heaven) to reward good deeds, the act of giving is still inherently good. The emphasis marker 'ஏ' in 'ஈதலே' stresses that giving is an absolute virtue, independent of any expectation of future rewards.

ai.literal: "I have nothing" which-says distress not-speaking giving, noble-birth he-who-possesses only-with they-exist.
ai.translation: The act of giving without ever uttering the distressing words "I have nothing" is found only in those of noble birth.
ai.modern: என்னிடம் ஒன்றும் இல்லை என்ற துன்பமான சொல்லைச் சொல்லாமல் பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்கும் பண்பு, நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்தவனிடமே இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the graciousness of a truly noble giver. When approached for help, refusing by saying "I have nothing" (இலன்) causes deep distress (எவ்வம்) to both the speaker and the seeker. The act of giving freely without ever uttering such painful words of refusal is a natural quality that exists (உள) only in those born of a noble, generous lineage (குலன் உடையான்). The word 'இலன்' here acts as direct speech, capturing the exact phrase of refusal that a noble person avoids.

ai.literal: Painful is being begged, until of those who begged the sweet face is seen.
ai.translation: Being asked for charity is painful only until you see the sweet, relieved face of the person who asked.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் வந்து யாசித்தவரின் மகிழ்ச்சியான முகத்தைக் காணும் வரைக்கும், ஒருவரால் யாசிக்கப்படுவது துன்பமானதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the emotional journey of giving. Initially, being approached by someone in need causes distress, as it highlights their suffering and places a burden on the giver. However, this pain lasts only until the giver provides what is needed. Once the giver sees the sweet, relieved face of the receiver, the initial distress transforms into joy.

ai.literal: The strength of those who endure is the enduring of hunger; (it is) behind the strength of those who relieve that hunger.
ai.translation: The strength of the strong is their ability to endure hunger, but it comes second to the strength of those who relieve the hunger of others.
ai.modern: பசியைப் பொறுத்துக்கொள்ளும் ஆற்றல் பெரியதுதான்; ஆனால் அது, மற்றவர்களின் பசியைப் போக்கும் கொடையாளர்களின் ஆற்றலுக்குப் பின்னால் தான் நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares two kinds of strength: the personal discipline to endure hunger, and the generosity to feed the hungry. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to those who have the power to withstand hardships. While enduring one's own hunger ('பசி ஆற்றல்') is a great strength, the poet places it 'behind' ('பின்') the strength of those who relieve ('மாற்றுவார்') the hunger of others. In this chapter on giving, this highlights that the act of sharing food is a far greater virtue than personal self-denial.

ai.literal: The destitute's ruinous hunger relieving, that is a man who acquired wealth's safe-keeping place.
ai.translation: Relieving the ruinous hunger of the destitute is the true safe-deposit for a man's acquired wealth.
ai.modern: ஏழைகளின் கொடிய பசியைத் தீர்ப்பதே, ஒருவன் தான் பெற்ற செல்வத்தைப் பாதுகாப்பாக வைக்கும் இடமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the most secure way to invest one's wealth. It states that relieving the devastating hunger of the destitute is the true safe-deposit for a person's riches. The term 'அழிபசி' highlights the destructive power of starvation, making its relief a vital act of charity. By comparing this act to a 'வைப்புழி' (treasury or safe-keeping place), the poet conveys that wealth given to the needy is never lost, but securely stored as enduring goodness.

ai.literal: having shared food having accustomed him hunger which is called evil disease touching is rare
ai.translation: The evil disease called hunger will rarely touch the man who is accustomed to sharing his food.
ai.modern: தன்னிடமுள்ள உணவை மற்றவர்களுடன் பகிர்ந்து உண்ணும் பழக்கம் உள்ளவனை, பசி என்று சொல்லப்படும் கொடிய நோய் தீண்டுவது இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the protective power of generosity. The phrase 'பாத்து ஊண் மரீஇ' describes someone who has made it a habit to share their food before eating. The poet personifies hunger as an 'evil disease' (தீப்பிணி), highlighting its destructive nature. However, this disease will rarely touch (தீண்டல் அரிது) the one who shares, suggesting that a generous person will always be provided for and protected from starvation.

ai.literal: Having given, the rejoicing joy do they not know, I wonder, who their own wealth having hoarded lose, the hard-hearted ones?
ai.translation: Do the hard-hearted, who hoard their wealth only to lose it, not know the joy that comes from giving and rejoicing?
ai.modern: தமது செல்வத்தை யாருக்கும் கொடுக்காமல் சேர்த்து வைத்துப் பின் அதனை இழந்துவிடும் வன்கண்மை உடையவர்கள், பிறருக்குக் கொடுத்து மகிழும் இன்பத்தை அறிய மாட்டார்களோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the pure joy of giving with the futility of hoarding. The phrase 'ஈத்து உவக்கும் இன்பம்' captures the happiness that comes from sharing with others and seeing them rejoice. The poet wonders ('கொல்') if those who are hard-hearted ('வன்கணவர்') are completely ignorant of this joy. These individuals merely hoard their possessions ('தாம் உடைமை வைத்து') without using them, ultimately losing everything. The word 'வன்கணவர்' specifically denotes those lacking the compassion to give, highlighting their emotional blindness to the joy of charity.

ai.literal: Than begging, is painful indeed, accumulated things oneself alone as a solitary person eating.
ai.translation: Eating one's hoarded wealth all by oneself is truly more painful than begging.
ai.modern: தான் சேர்த்து வைத்த பொருளைத் தான் மட்டுமே தனியாக இருந்து உண்பது, பிறரிடம் சென்று பிச்சை எடுப்பதை விட மிகவும் துன்பமானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the pain of begging with the act of hoarding wealth to consume it alone. The word 'இரத்தலின்' uses the ablative suffix to mean 'worse than begging', setting up a stark comparison. 'நிரப்பிய' refers to things that have been amassed or filled up over time. To eat these accumulated things entirely by oneself, expressed by the phrase 'தாமே தமியர் உணல்' (oneself as a solitary person eating), is declared to be 'இன்னாது' (painful or bad). The particle 'மன்ற' adds certainty, emphasizing that selfish hoarding without sharing is truly a more wretched state than being forced to beg.

ai.literal: Than dying, painful thing there is not; sweet is even that, giving not-possible time.
ai.translation: There is nothing more painful than dying, yet even death is sweet when it is no longer possible to give to others.
ai.modern: இறப்பதை விடத் துன்பமான செயல் வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை. ஆனால், பிறருக்குக் கொடுத்து உதவ முடியாத நிலை வரும்போது அந்த இறப்பும் இனிமையானதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the ultimate pain of death with the inability to be generous. The phrase 'சாதலின் இன்னாதது இல்லை' establishes that dying is universally considered the most painful experience. However, the poet flips this expectation by declaring that even death becomes sweet ('இனிது அதூஉம்'). This happens when one is in a state where giving to others is impossible ('ஈதல் இயையாக் கடை'). The poem emphasizes the supreme value of charity by making a life without it worse than death itself.
